1.title: Modules: Sources, Versions and the Registry
1.text: Welcome to Module eleven: Modules: Sources, Versions and the Registry. It covers the exam area five. Terraform modules. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. five A Explain how Terraform sources modules. five D Manage module versions. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: five. Terraform modules. Exam format: a one-hour online-proctored multiple-choice exam on Terraform one point one two. Validated against: the official Terraform Associate version oh oh four exam objectives.

1.title: What a module is
1.text: What a module is. A module is a container for several resources that are used together: a folder of dot tf files. Modules organize, encapsulate and reuse configuration.

1.title: What a module is, continued
1.text: What a module is. The figure shows this: The root module calls child modules from different sources.

1.title: What a module is, continued
1.text: What a module is. Root module. The configuration in the working directory where you run Terraform. Child module. A module called by another module with a module block. Published module. A module shared through a registry.

1.title: What a module is, continued
1.text: What a module is. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Every Terraform configuration is a module: the one you run is the root module.

1.title: Module sources
1.text: Module sources. The source argument tells Terraform where to get the module. It is required. Local path. . slash modules slash network or.. slash shared slash network (must start with. or or.. or ). Terraform Registry (public). terraform aws modules slash vpc slash aws (namespace or name or provider). Private registry (H C P Terraform). app dot terraform dot io slash my org slash network slash aws. Git Hub. github dot com slash my org slash terraform aws network. Generic Git. git H T T P S colon slash slash example dot com slash network dot git?ref v one dot two dot zero. H T T P U R L. An archive at a U R L. Cloud storage. S three or Google Cloud Storage buckets.

1.title: Module sources, continued
1.text: Module sources. Download. terraform init downloads modules into dot terraform slash modules. After a source change. Run terraform init again (or terraform get ). Registry naming. Modules are named terraform- P R O V I D E R - N A M E. Verified modules. The public registry marks modules reviewed by Hashi Corp partners.

1.title: Module versions
1.text: Module versions. Registry modules (public or private). The version argument with the same constraint syntax as providers ( about five dot zero, five dot one, six dot zero, five dot two dot zero ). Git. A tag, branch or commit with?ref. Local paths. No version: the files are whatever is on disk. The version argument works only with registry sources. Without it, Terraform uses the newest version on the first init. Pin module versions. Predictable infrastructure. Upgrade on purpose. Change the constraint and run terraform init -upgrade. Use semantic versions. Major changes may break, minor add, patch fix. Exam tip: version is for registry modules only. For a Git module use?ref; for a local module there is no version.

1.title: Why use modules
1.text: Why use modules. Reuse. Write once, call many times with different inputs. Encapsulation. Hide details behind inputs and outputs. Consistency. Same standards everywhere. Speed. Start from tested modules in the registry. Organization. Smaller, focused configurations. Exam tip: A module needs init before it works. Whenever a module block is added or its source changes, run terraform init again.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which source value refers to a module in a folder next to the root configuration? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: . slash modules slash network. Local paths must begin with. or or.. or.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team wants to pin a public registry module to any five.x version. What should they add to the module block? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: version equals "about greater than five point zero". The version argument takes a constraint such as about greater than five point zero and works for registry modules.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which command downloads the modules of a configuration? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: terraform init. terraform init downloads modules into the.terraform or modules directory.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A module comes from a Git repository. How can a team pin it to a release tag? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: With?ref equals in the source address. For Git sources the ref query parameter selects a tag, branch or commit.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. What is the root module? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The configuration in the working directory. The root module is the configuration in the directory where Terraform runs.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which statement about the version argument is correct? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: It works for registry modules only. The version argument is only valid for modules from a registry.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is a module? Answer: A container of resources used together, in a folder. Question two. What argument is required in a module block? Answer: source. Question three. What must a local path start with? Answer: . or or.. or.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Where are downloaded modules stored? Answer: .terraform or modules. Question five. Which sources accept the version argument? Answer: Registry sources only. Question six. How do you pin a Git module? Answer: With?ref equals in the source address.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Module: folder of.tf files; root module is the working directory. Sources: local path, registry, private registry, Git Hub, Git, H T T P, S three, G C S. Versions: version for registry modules only;?ref equals for Git; none for local. Commands: init downloads modules; init -upgrade moves to newer versions.
